source: The operator's decisions of 2026-09-26: D14, no posting more than a week old; D13, no posting he is not eligible for, and none missed that he is. Preferences are configuration under ADR-0031. Every place below is matched as whole words on the folded location text, never as a substring.
max_age_days_note: D14: 'i do not want a job post more than a week old', judged once, at first sight (his correction of 2026-09-26, ADR-0052): a posting first seen more than this many days after its publication date is dropped, and one admitted stays admitted however long it waits. A posting whose date is not proven to be a publication date (Lever's createdAt) is never dropped for age.
home_note: Places in Pakistan. A location naming one is eligible. Hyderabad is left out on purpose: India has one too, and 'Hyderabad, India' must not read as Pakistan.
home_country_note: Which of the home places is the country rather than a city. 'Pakistan (On-site)' names no city, so it may be Karachi and is kept; an on-site posting is out only when it names a home city other than Karachi. A dropped posting's reason names these, so it says what was absent without any module naming a country.
onsite_home_city_note: D13: 'any onsite post besides karachi, pakistan are automatically out'. A Pakistan location that says it is on site or hybrid is eligible only in these cities. One that says neither is kept, since whether it is on site cannot be read from it.
remote_note: Remote with no place named is eligible. Beside a country it is that country's remote, as in 'Remote, Germany', and closed. Beside an on-site word it is a remote option, as in 'Remote/Hybrid - Lahore', and eligible.
open_note: Worldwide, and regions that can include Pakistan. A location naming one is eligible even beside a closed country, as in 'US, Canada, Asia', unless it says only, as in 'Global (US only)', or scopes it, as in 'anywhere in the US'. D13: 'if they say that they are hiring from anywhere like worldwide or lets say no mention of a country then they should be filtered in'.
closed_note: Countries other than Pakistan, their common short forms, and regions that cannot include it. A location every part of which names one of these, and no home place, is out: 'if there is an ai engineer post from usa and it says only us people then i am out'. A part naming nothing known is kept, so an unrecognised spelling can only let a posting through, never lose one.
stated_levels_admitted_note: The operator, 2026-10-02: where a source states a posting's level, keep the ones up to mid ('keep till mid'). Himalayas states one on every posting, from its own six: Entry-level, Mid-level, Senior, Manager, Director, Executive; no employer board states one. A posting is kept when any level it states is one of these, his option A, so a role labelled both mid and senior is not lost; one that states none is kept. The title rule still runs. The level is not the job type: interns, contract, part-time, temporary and volunteer roles are all kept, on every source, his decision of the same day: volunteering 'might be a good opportunity and can become a stepping stone'.
